items.stem: Which of the following is part of a complete set of financial statements?

options.text: A statement of cash flows for the period
options.rationale: Correct: a statement of cash flows is one of the required statements.
A share-price chart is not a required financial statement.
Management biographies are not financial statements.

options.text: A list of the entity's customers
options.rationale: A customer list is not a required statement.

items.explanation: Correct: a statement of cash flows is one of the required statements.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO underlying concepts does IAS 1 require in preparing financial statements? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: financial statements (other than cash-flow information) are prepared on the accrual basis.

options.text: The going concern basis, unless the entity intends or needs to cease trading
options.rationale: Correct: statements are prepared on a going concern basis unless that is inappropriate.

options.text: The cash basis of accounting for all items
options.rationale: The accrual basis, not the cash basis, is required.

options.text: Recognising income only when dividends are declared
options.rationale: Income recognition follows accrual principles, not dividend declaration.

items.explanation: Correct: financial statements (other than cash-flow information) are prepared on the accrual basis.

items.stem: A company presents a single-line 'other income' that hides a large, unusual gain. Why can this breach presentation requirements?

options.text: Material items should be disclosed separately so users can understand performance; aggregating a material item can impair fair presentation
options.rationale: Correct: materiality requires separate presentation of significant items.

options.text: All income must be presented on one line
options.rationale: That is the opposite of the requirement.

options.text: Gains are never allowed to be presented
options.rationale: Gains are presented; the issue is hiding a material one.

options.text: Only losses need to be disclosed separately
options.rationale: Both material gains and losses warrant separate disclosure.

items.explanation: Correct: materiality requires separate presentation of significant items.
